docRequirement: `plugins-reference.md` § *Skills-directory plugins* binds us to in-place plugin discovery from a skills tree. `:376`: "Any folder under a skills directory that contains a `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` manifest is loaded as a plugin named `<name>@skills-dir` on the next session, with no marketplace and no install step. Scaffold one with `plugin init`. Unlike a marketplace install, the plugin is discovered in place rather than copied into the plugin cache." The disambiguation table fixes the three cases — `:382` `<skills-dir>/foo/SKILL.md` with no manifest is "A plain skill named `foo`"; `:383` `<skills-dir>/foo/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` is "A plugin `foo@skills-dir`, which can bundle its own skills, agents, hooks, and more". The scope table fixes exactly two roots: `:390` `~/.claude/skills/` = personal, loads "In every project"; `:391` `<cwd>/.claude/skills/` = project, "Only after you accept the workspace trust dialog for that folder", with `:395` requiring its MCP servers to go through "the same per-server approval as a project `.mcp.json`". `:402` forbids the ancestor walk for these specifically: they "load only from the `.claude/skills/` of the directory where you start Claude Code. They don't walk up to the repository root the way plain skills and commands do". `:409`: "There is no `uninstall` step because nothing was installed from a marketplace", the only removal being `:412` `claude plugin disable my-tool@skills-dir`. `:912` names the admin control: "Admins can block this source with `strictKnownMarketplaces` or by adding `{"source": "skills-dir"}` to `blockedMarketplaces` in managed settings."
current: The fork has no in-place plugin discovery of any kind; every plugin must be resolved through an install that stages a copy into the content-addressed plugin cache. (1) Every skills-directory scan in the fork is the single function `skillRecords` (`packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:266`-`:310`). It admits a folder only when `join(slugPath, 'SKILL.md')` exists (`:282`-`:283`), emits `kind: 'skill'` (`:290`), and never stats `.claude-plugin/`. It cannot emit anything else: `NativeCapabilityKind = Exclude<CapabilityKind, 'plugin'>` (`packages/shared/src/capabilities/types.ts:29`), and the module header states the rule outright — "No plugin cache/projection is read here (W7/W8)" (`native-sources.ts:18`). (2) It has five call sites, all in `buildNativeCapabilityInventory` (`native-sources.ts:880`): `:903` `~/.agents/skills` (`GLOBAL_AGENT_SKILLS_DIR`, `packages/shared/src/skills/storage.ts:34`), `:904` `<configDir>/skills`, `:949` `<workspaceRoot>/skills`, `:1016` `<cwd>/.nessy-agent/skills`, and `:1065` `<dir>/.agents/skills` per ancestor depth (`PROJECT_AGENT_SKILLS_DIR`, `storage.ts:37`). `.claude/skills` is scanned nowhere — `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.local.json` (`:1051`-`:1058`) and `.claude/rules` (`:971`, `:1108`) are read beside ours, `.claude/skills` is not; `grep -ran "claude/skills"` over `packages`+`apps` returns only comments and prose. (3) The single production consumer, `buildCapabilityResolutionInputsV2` (`packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:623`), takes exactly two capability inputs: the native inventory at `:635` and `deps.pluginStore.readInstalledRegistry()` at `:645`, whose active entries feed `resolvePluginProjectionCandidates(activeEntries, selectedScope)` at `:729`. There is no third, disk-discovered input. (4) Every route into that registry stages a copy: `PluginInstalledEntryV2` requires `cacheRef` (`packages/shared/src/plugins/store-v2.ts:42`-`:48`) and `install()` computes `bundleHash`, derives `cachePath = this.cachePathFor(cacheRef)` and calls `placeBundle` (`store-v2.ts:191`-`:200`). Even the `local-path` source kind (`packages/shared/src/plugins/types.ts:934`) runs through `createPluginStagingArea` (`packages/shared/src/plugins/source-resolver.ts:265`, used at `packages/shared/src/plugins/install-service.ts:279`) and `copyLocalPathArtifact` (`install-service.ts:539`) — a copy-with-install-step, the opposite of "discovered in place". (5) `PluginOriginSource` has no `skills-dir` member (`plugins/types.ts:35`-`:41`), and `store-v2.ts:193` defaults an unlabelled marketplace to `'local'`, so no plugin can ever be keyed `<name>@skills-dir` via `pluginKeyFor` (`packages/shared/src/workspaces/paths.ts:77`). (6) The documented admin control is rejected: the managed-policy classifier accepts only `github`/`url`/`hostPattern`/`pathPattern` and falls through to "declares an unsupported source" (`packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-marketplace-entries.ts:170`-`:206`); `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-marketplace-entries.test.ts:56` asserts that `{ source: 'skills-dir' }` in `strictKnownMarketplaces` is dropped as `strictKnownMarketplaces[3]`. (7) `grep -ran "reload-plugins\|reloadPlugins"` over `packages`+`apps` returns nothing, and `apps/cli/src/plugin.ts:132`-`:150` dispatches only `validate`/`list`/`ls`/`details`/`help` — there is no `disable` verb; `plugin init` is deliberately unimplemented and routed to `/create-plugin` (`apps/cli/src/plugin.ts:39`).
divergence: The whole mechanism is missing, not a key name or a value. Three separable deltas. (a) Discovery: no scanner ever stats `<skills-dir>/<name>/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`; `skillRecords` gates on `SKILL.md` alone (`native-sources.ts:282`), so a doc-conformant bundle — which per `:383` puts its skills at `<folder>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and need carry no root `SKILL.md` — contributes NOTHING. Only the subset that happens to also carry a root `SKILL.md` degrades to a bare skill with its agents/hooks/MCP silently dropped; the filed prose asserted that degraded case universally, which overstates one shape and understates the other. (b) Loading model: the doc's plugin is discovered in place and never enters the cache (`:376`), and has no uninstall because nothing was installed (`:409`); our only representation of a plugin is a cache-resident `PluginInstalledEntryV2` with a required `cacheRef` (`store-v2.ts:48`) placed by `install()` (`store-v2.ts:198`-`:200`). (c) Identity and control: `skills-dir` exists in neither `PluginOriginSource` (`plugins/types.ts:35`) nor the managed marketplace-source classifier (`managed-marketplace-entries.ts:170`-`:206`), so the key `<name>@skills-dir` cannot be produced and the documented `{"source": "skills-dir"}` admin switch is parsed as invalid and dropped. Also missing but subordinate: `/reload-plugins`, `plugin init`, and a `plugin disable` verb. Note the two roots the doc names (`~/.claude/skills/`, `<cwd>/.claude/skills/`) are not scanned at all in the fork under any name — the equivalent roots we do scan are `~/.agents/skills` and `<cwd>/.agents/skills` — so this is not a rebrand-path difference: the mechanism is absent whatever the directory is called.

change.what: In `skillRecords` (:266), probe `join(slugPath, '.claude-plugin', 'plugin.json')` BEFORE the `SKILL.md` gate at :282 and `continue` when it exists — a manifest-bearing folder is a plugin root, not a skill, so it must stop emitting `kind: 'skill'` (that is what makes `plugins/org.md#keep-skills-directory-plugins-loading (was line 382 of the retired plugins-reference page)` vs `:383` observable). Add an exported sibling `skillsDirPluginRoots(skillsDir, scope, discriminator, containRealRoot?): SkillsDirPluginRoot[]` that returns `{ logicalName, rootPath, manifestPath, scope }` for each such folder, reusing the existing `insideRealRoot` containment check (:241). Call it from `buildNativeCapabilityInventory` (:880) at EXACTLY two roots, mirroring the doc's scope table: the personal root beside :903 (`GLOBAL_AGENT_SKILLS_DIR`; add `join(homedir(), '.claude', 'skills')` too if the doc-literal path is also to be honoured) and the working directory's own skills dir inside the `projectTrustState === 'trusted'` branch (:995), which is already the trust gate `:391` requires. It must NOT go inside the ancestor loop at :1063-:1066 — `:402` explicitly forbids the walk-up for these plugins, unlike plain skills. Return them on a NEW `skillsDirPlugins` field of the returned `NativeCapabilityInventory` (:1135), never in `records`.

Add `interface SkillsDirPluginRoot { logicalName: string; rootPath: string; manifestPath: string; scope: CapabilityScopeRef }` and an additive `skillsDirPlugins: SkillsDirPluginRoot[]` field on `NativeCapabilityInventory`. Do NOT widen `NativeCapabilityKind` (:29) — it is `Exclude<CapabilityKind, 'plugin'>` by design and the whole native layer assumes it.
Add `'skills-dir'` to the union at :35-:41. One word, but every exhaustive `switch` over the union must gain the arm; typecheck will enumerate them.

Inside the existing safe-mode gate (:630) and after the registry read (:645), for each `discoveredNativeInventory.skillsDirPlugins` root call `normalizePluginBundle(rootPath, { source: 'skills-dir', marketplaceId: 'skills-dir', localPath: rootPath, resolvedAt: now })` (`packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters.ts:334`; the Claude adapter already parses this exact manifest — `format-adapters/claude.ts:145`, `:175`) and synthesize an EPHEMERAL `PluginInstalledEntryV2` per root with `pluginKey = pluginKeyFor('skills-dir', manifest.id)` (`packages/shared/src/workspaces/paths.ts:77`), a synthetic `pluginInstanceId`, and `bundleRootPath` set to the discovered folder. Concatenate onto `activeEntries` before `resolvePluginProjectionCandidates(...)` at :729 — that function reads only `entry.manifest`/`pluginKey`/`pluginInstanceId`/`bundleHash` (`packages/shared/src/plugins/projection-candidates.ts:139`-`:196`) and needs no change. Do NOT write these into `PluginInstalledRegistryV2`: keeping them registry-free is what makes `:409` ("no `uninstall` step because nothing was installed") true, and it avoids a persisted-schema change.

`pluginRuntimeRoots` (:242) already maps instance id to `plugin.bundleRootPath` from the snapshot, so an in-place root outside the cache is representable with no change. `verifyPlugin` (:137) is the one blocker: it recomputes `computeBundleHash(root)` and calls `stale()` on any mismatch (:145-:147), so a user-editable in-place bundle goes stale on the first save. Decide one of: recompute the expected hash per resolve for `skills-dir`-origin entries, or skip the integrity compare for them and record the reason in the constant. This is the design decision the rest of the change hangs on, and it is what makes `:405`'s split (SKILL.md edits live, other components need `/reload-plugins`) implementable.

Accept `{ "source": "skills-dir" }` as a valid entry instead of falling through to "declares an unsupported source" at :206, with `:912`'s polarity: present in `blockedMarketplaces` turns the scan OFF; present in `strictKnownMarketplaces` opts the scan back IN (any other allowlist blocks it). This is a security allowlist — get the polarity right or it widens.

change.symbol: 'strips an individual invalid entry and enforces the valid subset' (:50-:68)
change.what: Invert the `{ source: 'skills-dir' }` case: it currently asserts the entry is dropped as `strictKnownMarketplaces[3]` (:56, :64-:66). It must become a retained entry, and gain a companion case for `blockedMarketplaces`.

Also invalidate the capability generation when `<skills-dir>/*/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` appears or disappears; otherwise a newly scaffolded skills-directory plugin needs a full app restart rather than the doc's "on the next session".

NOTE ONLY, not required by this row: the switch dispatches only `validate`/`list`/`ls`/`details`/`help`, so `claude plugin disable my-tool@skills-dir` (`:412`) has no CLI equivalent and `plugin init` is deliberately routed to `/create-plugin` (:39). Disabling a discovered plugin has to work through the capability policy store instead; if it does not, discovery ships with no off switch.

blastRadius: `buildNativeCapabilityInventory` has exactly ONE production caller, `buildCapabilityResolutionInputsV2` (`packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:635`), whose output is the `CapabilityResolutionInputs` snapshot behind every agent turn's pinned capability context (`packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:95` imports the module). Direct test coverage of the inventory: `packages/shared/src/capabilities/__tests__/native-sources.test.ts`, `rules-tier.test.ts`, `nested-instruction-discovery.test.ts`. Other readers of the inventory shape: `packages/shared/src/capabilities/invalidation.ts:24`, `packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts`, `packages/shared/src/capabilities/project-contribution-detect.ts:21`. On the plugin side, `resolvePluginProjectionCandidates` (`packages/shared/src/plugins/projection-candidates.ts:139`) and `packages/shared/src/capabilities/materializer.ts` gain entries whose bundle root is outside the plugin cache — covered by `packages/server-core/src/sessions/__tests__/plugin-capability-runtime.test.ts`, `packages/shared/src/plugins/__tests__/store-v2.test.ts`, `management-service-v2.test.ts`. THREE boundaries are crossed and each is a risk trigger in this repo. (1) PERSISTENCE: if the ephemeral-entry route is abandoned in favour of registry rows, `PluginInstalledRegistryV2` (`store-v2.ts:63`, `schemaVersion: 2`) needs `cacheRef` to become optional — `readInstalledRegistry` (`store-v2.ts:161`) throws "Incompatible plugin registry schema; refusing to import" on any bump, so a version change is a hard migration. The recommended change avoids this; verify it stays avoided. (2) MANAGED POLICY / SECURITY: `managed-marketplace-entries.ts` is an org allowlist whose documented polarity is fail-closed (`settings.md:194`, quoted at `managed-marketplace-entries.test.ts:71`); a wrong arm silently widens what an org allows. (3) TRUST + WIRE: project-scope roots must stay behind `projectTrustState === 'trusted'` (`native-sources.ts:995`) and their MCP servers behind the existing per-server approval (`:395`); and if the UI is to show `<name>@skills-dir` provenance, the generated protocol types `packages/codex-protocol/generated/v2/PluginDetail.ts` and `SkillsListEntry.ts` change with it. Adding `'skills-dir'` to `PluginOriginSource` (`plugins/types.ts:35`) fans out to every exhaustive switch over the union across `packages/shared/src/plugins` and `packages/shared/src/marketplace`.
userImpact: A user who follows Claude's own docs and drops a plugin folder into a skills directory gets total silence. Concretely: create `~/.agents/skills/my-tool/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (or the doc-literal `~/.claude/skills/my-tool/...`) with bundled `agents/`, `hooks/` and `.mcp.json`, restart the app, and nothing appears anywhere — the Skills panel shows no `my-tool`, the plugin list shows no `my-tool@skills-dir`, the bundled agents/hooks/MCP servers/output styles never load, and no diagnostic is emitted, because `skillRecords` (`native-sources.ts:282`) simply `continue`s past a folder with no root `SKILL.md`. The only partially-visible variant is a bundle that also carries a root `SKILL.md`: then the skill text loads as a plain skill and every other component is dropped without a word. There is no error to search for, so the failure reads as "the app ignored my file". Secondary, latent: an org that ships `{"source": "skills-dir"}` in managed `blockedMarketplaces` gets a dropped-entry diagnostic instead of an enforced control (`managed-marketplace-entries.test.ts:56`) — harmless while the scan does not exist, but it will read as "policy applied" the moment it does, so the policy arm must land in the same change as the scan, not after it.

I confirmed the strings exist; I did NOT confirm the scan executes. If it does, a session on the Claude backend (opt-in, `NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE` off by default) may load `~/.claude/skills` plugins that the fork's own capability system knows nothing about — a per-backend inconsistency the host would not be able to display, disable, or gate on project trust. Worth one packaged-build measurement before choosing the design. THE ONE OPEN DESIGN CHOICE inside the change list is materializer integrity (item 5): whether to recompute or skip the bundle hash for an editable in-place bundle. Everything else follows once that is decided.
